Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1242 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Valid 301200Z - 311200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER A SMALL PART
OF SOUTH-CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA INTO CENTRAL NEBRASKA...

...SUMMARY...
Widely scattered severe storms capable of mainly damaging wind gusts
appear possible over south-central South Dakota into central
Nebraska Thursday afternoon and evening. More sporadic occurrences
of mainly damaging wind appear possible from the northern High
Plains into the upper Mississippi Valley into the central Plains,
the Raton Mesa vicinity, and the central and eastern Gulf Coast.

...Synopsis...

A short-wave trough initially over the northern Plains Thursday
morning will translate into the upper Midwest, while a trailing
disturbance moves through the mid MO Valley. Some enhancement of the
mid-level flow is forecast with the secondary system over the
central Plains. In the low levels, a surface low is expected to
track from SD into MN, along a cool front moving through the upper
MS Valley and the northern Plains into the central Plains. A
secondary low is forecast to deepen along the front over central KS.


...Northern High Plains into the upper Mississippi Valley and the
central Plains...

Latest model guidance continues to indicate showers and
thunderstorms ongoing at 12Z Thursday across the northern Plains
into the mid MO Valley, within a zone of forcing for ascent
preceding the lead short-wave trough. A subset of that convection
may linger into afternoon with associated cloud cover limiting
daytime heating and resultant destabilization. Where stronger
heating can occur, the presence of boundary-layer dewpoints in the
60s to low/mid 70s will contribute to MLCAPE up to 2000-3000 J/kg.

Thunderstorms are expected to increase in coverage and intensity
during the afternoon in the vicinity of the cool front and any
differential heating/outflow boundaries associated with previous
and/or active convection. A separate area of storms may also develop
later in the afternoon over eastern MT in the vicinity of a surface
low and lee trough. Damaging winds appear to be the primary hazard,
though isolated occurrences of large hail are also possible. 

A number of physics-based models and AI guidance indicate a corridor
from south-central SD into central or eastern NE as being a
preferred location for upscale growth of storms into a
cold-pool-driven MCS Thursday afternoon into evening, which would
enhance the damaging-wind potential. That scenario appears plausible
as the consensus of model guidance depicts that zone as having the
most favorable overlap of moderate to strong instability and modest
vertical shear. Given these considerations, a 15% wind probability
contour and related level 2/Slight Risk have been included to
account for that potential.

Enhanced moisture transport and storm-relative inflow along a
nocturnal low-level jet are likely to sustain a complex of storms
with some damaging wind risk Thursday night, mainly over eastern KS
into the mid MO Valley.


...Raton Mesa vicinity...

Convergence along the southward-moving front and/or upslope in its
immediate wake are expected to foster isolated to widely scattered
storms by mid afternoon along the high terrain. While vertical will
remain relatively weak, the presence of a steep-lapse-rate
environment, featuring a deep, well-mixed boundary layer will
support the potential for isolated severe wind gusts.


...Central and eastern Gulf Coast...

Early-day thunderstorms are expected across portions of the far
northeast Gulf and central FL Peninsula. To the north of that
convection, model guidance indicates a corridor of moderate to
strong instability developing by afternoon in the vicinity of a
stalled front. Diurnally enhanced thunderstorms are expected within
that zone of stronger air mass destabilization with steepening
low-level lapse rates and high precipitable water content supportive
of locally damaging wet microbursts.

..Mead.. 07/29/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0230 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Valid 301200Z - 311200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
THE NORTHERN TO CENTRAL PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Sporadic occurrences of mainly damaging wind appear possible
Thursday afternoon and night across parts of the northern and
central Plains.

...Discussion...
On Thursday, the pattern will feature an upper trough over the East
with filling low over the Northeast, and an upper high from the
Southwest into the Four Corners states. In between, a modest
northwest flow regime will exist over much of the Plains, with
embedded disturbances forecast over the northern and central Plains.

During the afternoon, a surface trough will develop from eastern MT
into the OK/TX Panhandles, where strong heating will occur. A
pre-frontal trough will also develop from SD into MN ahead of a cold
front trailing southwestward out of Ontario. This area may be
favorable timed with a weak wave moving around the upper ridge, and
storms that form within the surface trough will be capable of
sporadic severe hail or wind given 2000+ MUCAPE and deep-layer shear
around 30 kt. Possible early day thunderstorms complicate the
forecast setup, but a Slight Risk may eventually be added over the
northern Plains as predictability increases.

..Jewell.. 07/28/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0314 AM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Valid 311200Z - 051200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Friday...

The 00Z models have trended toward a more intense short-wave trough
over the Midwest, which in turn leads to a deeper surface low
tracking toward the mid MS Valley. However, the progression of those
features will be toward an area of more persistent surface ridging
with only an axis of modest instability forecast ahead of the
surface low. Stronger instability is expected to reside farther
southwest from the lower MO Valley into the Ozark Plateau, ahead of
a southeastward-moving cold front. A few severe storms appear
possible from the vicinity of the surface low southwest along the
cold front. But, given the northward displacement of the stronger
forcing for ascent and vertical shear from the stronger instability,
the degree of organized severe weather potential remains uncertain. 


Elsewhere, an isolated severe weather threat could materialize over
the northern and central High Plains within a moist, low-level
upslope regime.


...Day 5/Saturday...

The Day 4 short-wave trough is forecast to develop through the mid
MS into lower OH Valley along with the surface low. Meanwhile, the
trailing cold front will advance southeast into the lower MS Valley,
where moderate to strong instability is forecast by afternoon. A few
severe storms appear possible along and ahead of the front; however,
generally weak vertical shear is expected to limit the potential for
a more organized event. 

...Day 6-8/Sunday through Tuesday...

Both the ensemble means and deterministic models remain in
relatively good agreement in depicting a stronger short-wave trough
and attending belt of mid-level flow progressing along the
international border from the northern Rockies to the northern
Plains in the Sunday-Monday time frame. Some severe weather threat
could materialize along an associated cold front over ND on Sunday
and the northern Plains into the upper MS Valley on Monday as
strengthening vertical shear overspreads an unstable warm sector. By
Tuesday, the front is expected to stall over the central High Plains
with some severe weather threat possible within the post-frontal
upslope regime.

..Mead.. 07/28/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1213 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Valid 291200Z - 301200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OFTHE
NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS...AND FROM SOUTHERN GEORGIA INTO NORTHERN
FLORIDA....

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible this
afternoon and evening in the northern High Plains. Severe wind gusts
will also be possible today across southern Georgia and northern
Florida.

...Northern High Plains...
At mid-levels, a ridge will move eastward into the northern Plains
today. In the wake of the ridge, heights will begin to fall over the
northern High Plains. At the surface, a cold front will advance
southeastward into northwestern North Dakota and eastern Montana
this afternoon. Ahead of the front, surface dewpoints in the mid to
upper 50s F will contribute to moderate instability as surface
temperatures warm. Low-level convergence along the front will aid
convective initiation, with scattered thunderstorms moving eastward
across the western Dakotas during the late afternoon and early
evening.

RAP forecast soundings near the instability axis at 00Z have MLCAPE
in the 1500 to 2000 J/kg range. 0-3 km lapse rates are forecast to
be near 9 C/km with surface temperature-dewpoint spreads exceeding
40 degrees F. This should support a threat for severe wind gusts
with high-based storms that form ahead of the front. The potential
for severe gusts should be greatest in the early evening, especially
if a cold pool can organize across the northern High Plains. Hail
may also develop within the stronger cores.

...Southeast...
A mid-level trough will remain in place along the Eastern Seaboard
today, as a cold front advances southward into southern Georgia and
southern Alabama. To the south of the front, surface dewpoints in
the 70s F will contribute to an axis of strong instability by
afternoon, with MLCAPE likely peaking in the 3000 to 4500 J/kg
range. This, combined with 0-3 km lapse rates near 8 C/km, will be
favorable for damaging wind gusts. The greatest potential for severe
gusts will occur near the strongest instability, which is forecast
to be from southern Georgia into northern Florida.

..Broyles/Squitieri.. 07/29/2026
